# Campspot

**What this is:** the RV site booking and management platform — how RV sites are reserved, blocked and priced across the RV parks.

**Status:** current — 2026-08-30

## The facts
- **What they supply:** RV reservation and site management, plus reporting and analytics on RV bookings.
- **Who uses it:** on-site managers taking and blocking bookings, Sales and Marketing on RV occupancy and seasonal pricing, and Accounting and Asset Management on the reporting side. Rent Manager still holds the assets and the ledger — a River Oaks conversation records "there's still assets in Rent Manager… still sell it through Rent Manager" alongside Campspot for the site bookings.
- **What it is for, per the March board deck:** the 2026 RV goal is to "in-fill RV sites with park models and **generate incremental revenues from Campspot**." It is a revenue line, not just a booking tool.
- **How critical: high for the RV half of the portfolio.** RV is a large part of the estate — the 2026 JREFI infill plan is **104 park model RV sites against 85 MH lots** — and lighter RV occupancy in 2025 accounted for roughly **60% of a $920k rental income miss**, concentrated at River Oaks, Vantage Oaks, Lucky Clover and Paradise Lakes. Campspot is the only system that takes an RV booking; without it the RV parks have no reservation channel and the seasonal pricing strategy has nothing to run in.
- **Blocking sites is the control, and it is being used to fix a revenue leak.** At the Florida Whispering Pines on 2026-08-20: short-term bookings on Campspot were tying up lots meant for long stays, **small units were landing on the large 50-amp sites**, and the system would not let a long-term resident be booked past 2026.
- **The decision taken there: a six-month minimum stay on the sites historically used for full-season rentals, reducible to three months if bookings are slow, with the smaller west side sites kept open for short-term traffic — and the season sites blocked in Campspot** so small units stop occupying the large lots.
- The March deck also puts Campspot on the reporting agenda: **"CampSpot Analytics & Reporting — are we getting what we need from the platform?"** — an open question, not a settled answer.
- RV marketing sits alongside it and is not yet built: the deck's RV slide names Triple S with **12 vacant RV sites heading into season** and asks for the immediate plan, plus the status and launch timeline of a **standalone RV website and Parakeet Retreats page**.
- Campspot is also of commercial interest beyond being a vendor: a 2026-08-20 conversation records "we're looking at buying into Camp Spot too," with the company described as founded by the Workampers group, sold to private equity, and generating around $2m of EBITDA at about a $100m sale price — **as spoken on a recording, not a verified figure.**
- **Known problems — RV is the least-documented part of the company.** There is **no Campspot SOP anywhere**, and no RV process at all: SOPs 801, 802 and 804 explicitly exclude or route RV parks — "RV parks are Chapter 513 — no prospectus applies; route to Legal" — and **no Chapter 513 / RV compliance SOP exists**. RV appears in the operating SOPs only as a $500 checkbox on the eviction intake form.
- There is no RV collections path in SOP 100, no RV booking, cancellation, seasonal-rate or site-blocking procedure, and no statement of who owns the Campspot account. The 600s Systems band is empty.

## Decisions
- 2026-08-20 — Set a six-month minimum stay on the sites historically used for full-season rentals, with flexibility down to three months if bookings are slow, keeping the smaller west side sites short-term; block the season sites in Campspot. (Source: [[70-Operations/meetings/2026-08-southeast-tour/2026-08-20-whispering-pines-mh-and-rv-site-visit]])
